outcome: Since 26 January 2024 one dimension outside the bullet's exceptions has an exact value: a 2025 preprint by Dutour Sikirić and van Woerden (arXiv:2508.20719, 28 Aug 2025) reports γ₉ = 2 and that the laminated lattice Λ₉ is the densest lattice packing in dimension 9; I found no journal reference for it. Every other dimension the bullet covers (n = 10–23 and n ≥ 25) still has no exact value in any source I found. Bound-level work (Klartag 2025; Abuya, Gargava and Zhao 2026, with GPT-5.5 Pro) and an unreviewed density-function hypothesis (Lyalin 2026) touch the other dimensions only through bounds or approximations.
problem_asks: Written from the statement alone, before weighing events. (1) For every integer n ≥ 1 other than 1–8 and 24 (that is n = 9, 10, 11, …, 23, 25, 26, … with infinitely many parts), determine the Hermite constant γₙ. (2) Each part asks for the value, meaning the exact number, not a bound: the bullet says 'values'. (3) The quantity is the Hermite constant as the Wikipedia article defines it (a supremum over lattices of a normalised shortest-vector length). The bullet does not restate the definition, so I did not reconstruct it beyond that. The parts, dimension by dimension: n = 9; n = 10 to 23 (fifteen dimensions); n ≥ 25 (infinitely many). The first is the only one with an event below that claims an exact value.

events.what_happened: Mathieu Dutour Sikirić and Wessel van Woerden, ‘The lattice packing problem in dimension 9 by Voronoi’s algorithm’, arXiv:2508.20719. They compute all 2,237,251,040 perfect lattices in dimension 9 via Voronoi’s algorithm, classify 7,338,582 extreme lattices, conclude that the laminated lattice Λ₉ is the densest lattice packing in dimension 9, and state ‘Equivalently, we show that the Hermite constant γ₉ in dimension 9 equals 2’. They also classify the possible kissing numbers in dimension 9 as 2·{1,…,91,99,120,…,129,136}, extending Watson (1971). Van Woerden gave a seminar on it at Bordeaux on 30 Sep 2025. v2 (7 Feb 2026) adds a dedication to Jacques Martinet (1939–2026); I did not compare v1 and v2 line by line.
events.revisions: v1 28 Aug 2025; v2 7 Feb 2026 (adds dedication to Jacques Martinet per the v2 HTML; I did not confirm whether any stated result changed).
events.delivers: Exact value γ₉ = 2 for the Hermite constant in dimension 9, equivalently Λ₉ is the densest lattice packing in dimension 9 (up to similarity, the classification is complete). The authors also note that γ₈ = γ₉ = 2. Restricted to dimension 9; it is one part of the bullet's infinite family.
events.remains: Every other part of problem_asks: γₙ for n = 10–23 and for n ≥ 25. The result does not touch them.
events.time_since_posted: About 13.5 months to 13 Oct 2026 (v1 28 Aug 2025). No journal reference, referee report, published review or expert commentary found. The only later public use is the citation and reliance in Gargava (July 2026), listed under later_work_cites_it, which uses the result as an input rather than checking it.
events.directly_checkable: The complete classification is cited as a Zenodo record (‘Complete classification of perfect lattices in dimension 9’) and the authors’ C++ implementation is public (Polyhedral repositories cited in the paper). I did not download either. The paper describes exhaustive enumeration with exact arithmetic in its eutaxy computations and does not describe formal (Lean or Coq) or certified verification of the count.
events.direction: Settles one part of the problem in the direction the bullet implies, an exact value. Nothing in the text contradicts a conjectured value for n = 9; I could not read the Mächler–Naccache Table 2 value for n = 9 to compare.
events.object: Not an exhibited object in the sense of a counterexample. The optimal object is the laminated lattice Λ₉ (the Korkine–Zolotarev lattice in later citations), identified as the densest lattice packing in dimension 9, with the squared minimal length 2 at determinant 1 (normalisation as cited by Gargava 2026). The proof of optimality is an exhaustive computer enumeration of perfect lattices, not an explicit existence result.

ai.disclosed_cost: Compute: parallel runs on 64–256 processes for a few days at a time, high-incidence cases on 16–256 cores, about 150 GB compressed output; run on the Curta cluster (MCIA) and the Lisa cluster (SURF). Stated in the paper.

events.what_happened: Cited in the Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden paper, in its own words: ‘Concurrent to this work, such a computation was also performed by Gregory Minton [60], up to a kissing number of 2·70, during which he found 2 237 251 031 perfect forms.’ Reference [60] is ‘Partial enumeration of perfect forms in dimension 9. Note: Personal correspondence.’ No public Minton source found in any search.
events.delivers: A partial enumeration of 9-dimensional perfect forms up to kissing number 2·70, reporting 2,237,251,031 perfect forms, against 2,237,251,040 in the full count. As reported, it does not establish any value of γ₉ on its own, and it is not publicly available to me.
events.remains: Everything in problem_asks. As far as I could find, no public result by Minton on γₙ.
events.time_since_posted: Not established; the only trace is the 2025 citation in the Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden paper.
events.direction: Consistent with the 2,237,251,040 count in the main paper; the two counts differ by nine forms, which the reported partial enumeration explains by being incomplete.

events.what_happened: Nihar Gargava, ‘On two counterexamples in the geometry of numbers’, arXiv:2607.11695 (math.MG), 13 Jul 2026. Neighbouring question, not the Hermite constant: it gives an exact counterexample in dimension 8 to a Cassels/Zong product problem for critical determinants and lattice packings (a rotated E8 gives a packing of B⁴×B⁴ of density π⁴/1024·(1+1/√5)⁴ ≈ 0.4173, above π⁴/256 from D4⊕D4), and a numerical counterexample in dimension 9 to a height question about flat tori (Sarnak, formulated as a conjecture by Chiu), built as a perturbation of Λ₉. The paper cites Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden as [10] and states their result as Theorem 15 (‘Up to similarity, the Korkine-Zolotareff lattice Λ9 is the unique densest nine-dimensional lattice packing’), noting in Remark 3 that [6] and [10] are ‘available only as preprints’. Its acknowledgements say the counterexamples were found by the AI system named below.
events.delivers: Neighbouring result, not a value of γₙ. In dimension 8, an exact counterexample to the unrestricted product formula for a Cassels/Zong problem. In dimension 9, a numerical counterexample to a Chiu conjecture on heights of flat tori. Neither gives a Hermite constant value, and the paper does not connect either to γₙ.
events.remains: All of problem_asks. The paper uses γ₉ = 2 only as an input (Theorem 15) and does not derive or extend any γₙ.
events.directly_checkable: The dimension 8 counterexample is an explicit lattice packing (rotated E8 against D4⊕D4 products), checkable by hand from the density formula the paper gives. The dimension 9 counterexample is a numerical perturbation of Λ₉ reported in floating point without interval certification, per the paper. The ancillary files include reproduction scripts, which I did not open.
events.doubts: The dimension 9 counterexample is numerical, in floating point without interval certification, as the paper itself states. That bears on the height question, not on γ₉.
events.direction: On the neighbouring questions, the two counterexamples cut against conjectured product formulas and a height conjecture. Neither cuts against any Hermite constant value.
events.object: Dimension 8: rotated E8 gives an explicit lattice packing of B⁴×B⁴ with density π⁴/1024·(1+1/√5)⁴ ≈ 0.4173, exceeding the product value π⁴/256 from D4⊕D4 (exact). Dimension 9: a one-parameter determinant-preserving deformation of Λ₉ that lowers the height (numerical).

systems.name: ChatGPT 5.5 Pro
systems.what_it_did: Per the author, found both counterexamples. The author writes that the model ‘developed the numerical methods to compute heights of lattices by itself’, supplied the correct rotation for the E8 lattice, and found ‘the right perturbation to deform Λ9 to obtain a counterexample’.
systems.basis_quote: The counterexamples were found using ChatGPT 5.5 Pro in various chat sessions.

events.what_happened: Elisha B. Abuya, Nihar Gargava and Yufei Zhao, ‘Stochastically evolving ellipsoids with symmetries’, arXiv:2606.05105. They prove that there is a universal constant c > 0 such that along an infinite sequence of dimensions N there are lattice sphere packings in ℝᴺ with density at least c·N²·log log N·2^(−N), improving Klartag’s c·N²·2^(−N) by a log log N factor. The proof follows Klartag’s stochastic ellipsoid process with Venkatesh’s cyclotomic symmetries. The authors’ own AI-use statement says the third author prompted GPT-5.5 Pro, which proposed combining the symmetries with Klartag’s method and proved the bound, and that ChatGPT and Codex were used extensively. The first author uses a pseudonym, per the paper. The paper does not mention γₙ or the Hermite constant; the bearing on γₙ is through the standard density relation, which I did not verify in an opened source.
events.delivers: A lattice packing density lower bound along an infinite, sparse sequence of dimensions, improving Klartag’s bound by a log log factor. Under the standard relation between packing density and γₙ (γₙ = 4(Δₙ/Vₙ)^(2/n), taken from a search summary and not checked in an opened source), this is a lower bound on γ_N along that sequence. It is not an exact value and it does not settle any dimension.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: no exact γₙ is given for any n, and the bound is for density along a subsequence of dimensions.
events.time_since_posted: About 4 months to 13 Oct 2026. No public engagement found beyond the arXiv listing.
events.direction: Lower-bound direction only. It pushes a lower bound on density, and by the relation above a lower bound on γ_N, upward. It contradicts no value.
events.object: Lattice sphere packings from Klartag’s stochastic ellipsoid evolution with Venkatesh’s cyclotomic symmetries. The existence argument is non-constructive: the origin-symmetric ellipsoid process yields a lattice, and no explicit lattice is given in the parts I read.
people: Elisha B. Abuya (a pseudonym, per the paper’s own note)
Yufei Zhao (third author, per author order)

systems.name: GPT-5.5 Pro
systems.what_it_did: Proposed combining Venkatesh’s cyclotomic symmetries with Klartag’s stochastic ellipsoid method, discovered the idea of letting the rank grow, and proved the bound stated in the paper. The authors say the model ‘produced an improvement over the previous best bound’ after further prompting.
systems.basis_quote: The model discovered the idea of letting the rank grow and successfully proved the bound given below.

systems.name: ChatGPT
systems.what_it_did: The ancillary files contain a log of the ChatGPT conversation that led to the proof. The paper does not say which model ran that conversation, so it is not established whether it is the same system as GPT-5.5 Pro.
systems.basis_quote: The ancillary files accompanying this paper include a complete log of the ChatGPT conversation that led to the proof.

events.what_happened: Boaz Klartag, ‘Lattice packing of spheres in high dimensions using a stochastically evolving ellipsoid’, arXiv:2504.05042, 7 Apr 2025. He proves that in every dimension n there is a lattice sphere packing with density at least c·n²·2^(−n) for a universal c > 0, improving earlier constructions of order n·log n·2^(−n). Quanta reported it on 7 Jul 2025 as ‘posted online in April’. Neither the abstract nor the Quanta article mentions the Hermite constant or AI.
events.delivers: A universal lower bound on lattice packing density in every dimension, c·n²·2^(−n). Through the same standard relation, a lower bound on γₙ in every dimension. Not an exact value for any n.
events.time_since_posted: About 18 months to 13 Oct 2026. Covered by Quanta (journalism, not a verification). The later bound by Abuya, Gargava and Zhao builds on it.
events.direction: Lower-bound direction only; it is consistent with every γₙ value.
events.object: Existence of a lattice sphere packing with density at least c·n²·2^(−n), from a stochastically evolving origin-symmetric ellipsoid that contains only the origin as a lattice point. Non-constructive.

events.what_happened: Maksim Lyalin, ‘Approximate Method for Solving the Problem of Lattice Packing of Equal Spheres in N−Dimensional Euclidean Space’, Preprints.org, DOI 10.20944/preprints202605.0225.v1. The abstract says that extending regularities of the layered ‘Lambda’ lattice packings in dimensions 1–24 led to a hypothesis about the density function of the densest lattice packing in n dimensions, offered as an approximate method. No proof. The full text was not available to me (HTTP 403).
events.delivers: A hypothesis, not a theorem, giving an approximate density for the densest lattice packing in every dimension. Through the standard relation, approximate values of γₙ. It states no exact value, and the abstract does not say how the hypothesis was tested beyond the layered series.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, and it leaves exact values open by its own description.
events.time_since_posted: About 5 months to 13 Oct 2026. The PREreview page showed 0 reviews.
events.doubts: Presented as a hypothesis and an approximate method, with no proof and no visible review. The search summary said the page is marked ‘not peer reviewed’; my fetch of the PREreview page did not show that label, so I have not confirmed it.
events.direction: Approximate, not exact. It does not contradict any value.

events.what_happened: OpenAI’s ‘Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science’ (1 Aug 2026) includes a sphere-packing result: the exact asymptotic exponential rate of the Cohn–Elkies linear programming bound, reported as an improved general sphere-packing upper bound in high dimensions. Press credits an internal model called Astra. The Lean repository is openai/ten-proofs; its README lists the sphere-packing result as ‘Improved asymptotic upper bounds on sphere-packing density, reaching the Cohn–Elkies threshold.’ The paper is not about lattices or the Hermite constant. The primary PDF (cdn.openai.com) was unreadable to me, so the attribution rests on press and the README.
events.delivers: Neighbouring result. An asymptotic upper bound for general (not necessarily lattice) sphere packing density, from the Cohn–Elkies LP method. It gives no Hermite constant value and no lattice value.
events.time_since_posted: About 2.5 months to 13 Oct 2026. The package was not peer reviewed as of 1 Aug. Lean formalisations exist; I did not examine them.
events.direction: Upper-bound direction for general sphere packing. It does not bear on the Hermite constant in any dimension in the bullet.

ai.disclosed_cost: Press reports about $2,000 for solution-search tokens across all ten problems. Not checked against OpenAI’s own text.

events.what_happened: Hariharan, Birkbeck, Lee, Ma, Mehta, Poiroux and Viazovska, ‘Progress in Formalizing Sphere Packing in Dimension 8’, arXiv:2604.23468 (v1 25 Apr 2026, v3 29 May 2026). The paper formalises Viazovska’s 2016 dimension-8 sphere packing proof in Lean. Its abstract says ‘the final stages of the verification [were] done by Math, Inc.’s autoformalization model ‘Gauss’’. Gauss also completed the dimension-24 formalisation according to EPFL and Scientific American. These are formalisations of results already proved by humans, for dimensions 8 and 24, which the bullet excludes.
events.delivers: A machine-checked formalisation of the known dimension-8 sphere packing result. Not a new value and not in the bullet’s scope: dimension 8 is excluded.
events.direction: Not relevant to the bullet’s open dimensions.

events.what_happened: Rasul Tutunov, Alexandre Maraval, Antoine Grosnit, Xihan Li, Jun Wang, Haitham Bou-Ammar, ‘Model-Based and Sample-Efficient AI-Assisted Math Discovery in Sphere Packing’, arXiv:2512.04829 (4 Dec 2025; v2 8 Dec 2025). They use Bayesian optimisation with Monte Carlo Tree Search to construct semidefinite programs for the three-point method, reporting new upper bounds for general (non-lattice) sphere packing in dimensions 4–16. Neighbouring result, not lattice and not Hermite.
events.delivers: Upper bounds on non-lattice sphere packing density in dimensions 4–16. No Hermite constant value and no lattice bound.
events.direction: Upper-bound direction for non-lattice packings in dimensions 4–16. Does not bear on the Hermite constant.

events.what_happened: Ruitao Chen, Jiachen Hu, Binghui Li, Liwei Wang, Tianyi Wu, ‘New Sphere Packings from the Antipode Construction’, arXiv:2505.02394 (5 May 2025). Non-lattice sphere packings in dimensions 19, 20, 21, 23, 44, 45 and 47 with record densities. The construction applies the antipode method to cross-sections of Λ₂₄ and P₄₈ₚ. Neighbouring result: explicitly non-lattice and not a Hermite constant value.
events.delivers: Non-lattice record packing densities in dimensions 19, 20, 21, 23, 44, 45 and 47. No value of γₙ, and no lattice packing claim.
events.direction: Non-lattice, so not on the Hermite constant.

events.what_happened: Boon Suan Ho, ‘A new lower bound for the kissing number in 19 dimensions’, arXiv:2603.10425 (v1 11 Mar 2026, v2 20 Mar 2026). It proves the kissing number in dimension 19 is at least 11948. This concerns kissing numbers, not the Hermite constant. A search snippet says the acknowledgements credit GPT-5.4 Pro; the abstract page I opened contains no AI sentence, and I did not open the full text, so I have not confirmed that.
events.revisions: v1 11 Mar 2026; v2 20 Mar 2026 (corrected errors, improved exposition).
events.delivers: A kissing-number bound in dimension 19. Not the Hermite constant and not a lattice packing density.
events.direction: Kissing-number direction only; no bearing on γₙ.
events.object: A binary code of length 19 and minimum distance 5 within the 5-punctured extended binary Golay code, with 1280 words, from which the kissing configuration is built (per the abstract).

events.what_happened: Leon Mächler and David Naccache (ENS-PSL), ‘A Conjecture on Hermite Constants’, Cryptology ePrint 2022/677. They note that (4/γₙ)ⁿ matches the minimal determinants of n-dimensional integral lattices with minimal length 4 for the known n, and conjecture that γₙⁿ for n = 9,…,23 takes the values in their Table 2. They also claim a provable lower bound on the Hermite constant for 1 ≤ n ≤ 24. The table and the lower-bound formula were not visible to me, since the PDF returned binary.
events.delivers: A conjecture of exact values for n = 9–23 (not a theorem), plus an asserted provable lower bound for n ≤ 24. Confined to the conjectured values; no value is proved.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as a conjecture: if the conjecture held it would settle n = 10–23 individually, but nothing is proved.
events.doubts: Conjectural. The pattern is observed from known values in dimensions 1–8 and 24, and the authors say the same coincidence fails at n = 24 for µ = 2, which led them to µ = 4. Whether the Table 2 value for n = 9 agrees with the Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden result I could not check.
events.direction: Conjectural values for n = 9–23; direction cannot be stated until the table is read.

events.what_happened: Yoav Kallus, ‘Statistical mechanics of the lattice sphere packing problem’, arXiv:1305.1310, 6 May 2013; Phys. Rev. E 87, 063307 (2013). A Monte Carlo method that, per the abstract, ‘numerically discover[s] de novo the densest lattice sphere packing in dimensions 9 through 20’. Numerical, not a proof, and it does not mention the Hermite constant in the abstract.
events.delivers: Numerical identification of candidate densest lattices in dimensions 9–20. Through the standard relation, candidate γₙ values. Not a proof of any value.
events.doubts: Numerical. The abstract says the method found the densest lattices but does not claim a proof.
events.direction: Candidate values, numerically. I did not check whether Kallus’s dimension-9 candidate is Λ₉; the 2025 Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden paper proves Λ₉ is the densest, so a comparison is possible but not made here.
events.object: Numerically found densest lattice packing in each dimension 9–20 (the candidate lattices themselves are not listed in the abstract).

events.what_happened: Hao Chen, ‘New lattice sphere packings denser than Mordell-Weil lattices’, arXiv:1110.1950, v1 10 Oct 2011 (v5 31 May 2012); published as ‘On a generalization of Craig lattices’, JTNB 2013. The abstract says lattice packings in dimensions 3332–4096 are denser than known Mordell-Weil packings, and lists improvements in dimensions 4098–8232 and 84, 85, 86 and 181–189. The abstract does not mention γₙ.
events.delivers: Lower bounds on lattice packing density, hence on γₙ, in the listed dimensions (the search snippets garble the exact ranges; the abstract is the source I checked). Not exact values.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: no exact value in any listed dimension.
events.object: Lattice packings constructed from generalised Craig lattices, in the dimensions listed above.

events.what_happened: Roland Bacher, ‘A new inequality for the Hermite constants’, arXiv:math/0603477, submitted 20 Mar 2006, last revised 23 Jan 2007. Proves γₙ ≥ Cₙ(γₙ₋₁) for a function Cₙ, and derives a new proof of the Minkowski–Hlawka bound.
events.delivers: A lower bound on each γₙ in terms of γₙ₋₁. No value.

events.what_happened: Jinming Wen, Xiao-Wen Chang and Jian Weng, ‘Improved Upper Bounds on the Hermite and KZ Constants’, arXiv:1904.09395, 20 Apr 2019. Gives a linear upper bound on the Hermite constant, and an upper bound on the KZ constant derived from it. The explicit form and the dimensions it applies to were not visible in the abstract.
events.delivers: An upper bound on γₙ, linear in n, in the form the abstract describes. Not a value.

events.what_happened: Jinming Wen and Xiao-Wen Chang, ‘Sharper Bounds on Four Lattice Constants’, arXiv:2204.08021, 17 Apr 2022, ‘to appear in Designs, Codes and Cryptography’. Develops a linear upper bound on Hermite’s constant, an upper bound on the KZ constant, and lower and upper bounds on Schnorr’s and Rankin’s constants. Search snippets report a ratio to Blichfeldt’s 1929 bound tending to about 1.0047 and that the linear bound beats the earlier one only for dimension at least 109; I did not verify these in the opened abstract.
events.revisions: v1 only, per the arXiv page I opened.
events.delivers: A sharper upper bound on γₙ than the 2019 bound. Not a value.

events.what_happened: Björn Muetzel, ‘A new lower bound for Hermite’s constant for symplectic lattices’, arXiv:1105.2752, 13 May 2011 (v2 12 Dec 2011). Improves the lower bound for the symplectic Hermite constant δ₂g in even dimensions, and gives symmetric lattices in dimensions that are powers of two. This is an analogue (a symplectic variant), not γₙ.
events.delivers: A lower bound for the symplectic Hermite constant δ₂g in even dimensions. An analogue, so it settles nothing here.
events.direction: Concerns the symplectic analogue; no direction on γₙ.

disputes.summary: Not contested in any source, but worth the later pass’s attention. Dutour Sikirić and van Woerden say that Gregory Minton performed a concurrent partial enumeration of 9-dimensional perfect forms, citing personal correspondence. I found no public record of Minton’s work, and no source says the two computations were cross-checked. The full count of 2,237,251,040 rests on the Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden paper alone in the public record.

summary: The only event in this record that gives an exact value of γₙ for a dimension in the bullet’s range is the Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden preprint (arXiv:2508.20719, first posted 28 Aug 2025; v2 7 Feb 2026). It completes Voronoi’s algorithm in dimension 9, enumerating all 2,237,251,040 perfect lattices, and concludes γ₉ = 2 with Λ₉ the densest lattice packing. I read its full HTML text for both halves and found no AI mention. It describes exhaustive computation with exact arithmetic in the eutaxy checks, and it does not describe formal or certified verification. I found no journal reference, no referee report, and no expert write-up. The public uses are the later Gargava paper (arXiv:2607.11695, July 2026), which cites it as [10] and states Λ₉’s uniqueness as its Theorem 15, and the Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden paper’s own citation of a partial concurrent enumeration by Minton (personal correspondence). Close calls: (a) Counting, as a resolution, a single exact value in an infinite family. The bullet asks for all values, so this is one part settled, not the problem. The bullet’s own rule treats a single case settled as an event, and I have recorded it that way. (b) Whether bound-level work counts. The bullet asks for values, but Klartag (April 2025) and Abuya, Gargava and Zhao (June 2026) move lattice density lower bounds, and by the standard relation γₙ = 4(Δₙ/Vₙ)^(2/n) (taken from a search summary, not an opened source) those are lower bounds on γₙ along all dimensions or along a sparse sequence. I recorded them and did not treat them as settling anything. (c) The Lyalin preprint (Preprints.org, 5 May 2026) is a hypothesis for an approximate density, not a proof; its full text returned HTTP 403, so its AI involvement is unknown. AI involvement, recorded by source. The one AI-attributed event bearing on the bullet itself is the Abuya–Gargava–Zhao paper, which says GPT-5.5 Pro proposed the idea and proved the density bound, and that a ChatGPT conversation led to the proof. That is load-bearing for a lattice density bound along a sparse sequence of dimensions, not for any γₙ value, and the paper does not mention γₙ. The Gargava paper credits ChatGPT 5.5 Pro with finding its two counterexamples, which are about neighbouring questions. The OpenAI ‘Astra’ sphere-packing result (1 Aug 2026) and the Gauss-assisted dimension-8 formalisation are about general sphere packing and about dimension 8, which the bullet excludes. Huawei/UCL (Dec 2025) is AI-assisted but names no system and concerns non-lattice upper bounds. Its Bayesian-optimisation and MCTS method is not an LLM. Cited-but-unread: the Mächler–Naccache table (γₙⁿ for n = 9–23) and the Nguyen chapter, both binary PDFs. The Wikipedia Hermite constant article (last revision 6 Mar 2026) still lists exact values only for dimensions 1–8 and 24 and does not mention the 2025 dimension-9 result. The Wikipedia list’s bullet for this problem links to that article, under the ‘Euclidean geometry’ heading. Dimensions 10–23 and 25 onward: no exact value found. No 2026 result on any γₙ, n ≠ 9, was found in 39 searches and the opened sources.
competing_reading: The strongest case for a different reading: (1) Under the Dutour Sikirić–van Woerden paper, the problem is not settled in any meaningful sense, since 1 dimension out of infinitely many is a single part, and a reader might treat a bound-level-only record as no progress; that reading makes the 2025 event a partial settlement rather than a resolution. (2) Against treating the 2025 event as solid: the paper is an unreviewed preprint with a computation that is not formally verified, and a partial concurrent enumeration (Minton) is cited without public data. A reader who wants a higher bar could count the result as pending until a journal or an independent computation confirms the count. (3) On the AI side, a reader could take the Abuya–Gargava–Zhao AI-use statement as making the density bound AI-generated in substance, which would matter if the judging pass counts lattice density bounds as part of this bullet; the bullet asks for values, so I do not think it does.
what_would_settle_it: (a) A journal reference or referee report for arXiv:2508.20719, or an independent recomputation of the 9-dimensional perfect lattice count (or the public Minton data, if it exists). (b) The Mächler–Naccache Table 2 value for n = 9, to check the conjecture against γ₉ = 2. (c) Any exact value in dimension 10 to 23 or 25 and up, or a survey confirming none exists. (d) For the AI attribution in the Abuya–Gargava–Zhao paper, the ancillary chat log, to establish whether the ChatGPT conversation that led to the proof was run on GPT-5.5 Pro. (e) The Lyalin full text and its AI-use statement, if any. (f) The Mächler–Naccache PDF, for the lower-bound formula and the table.
